Patrick Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion, the lowest in the league, and went 0-for-4 on throws of ten or more yards. In full PPR the slot is where receptions live, so being pushed outside is the part that hurts. He still starts: one game, Kansas City implied 27.0 at home, the knee entirely off the Week 2 injury report, and the bench alternative is Devaughn Vele playing against my own defence. This is a flag, not a move, and it is on the record now so it is not re-discovered next week.
open.falsifiedIf: A second week under 15% target share, or the slot rate staying at 25% through Week 3. Two weeks of that is a role change and makes him a sell-high trade candidate rather than an untouchable. Conversely a normal Week 2 line closes this row and the Week 1 usage was the game script.

PROCESS ERROR REPEATED, and it is the second time. The closed entry dated 16 Sep 06:10 already records this exact failure and ends 'LESSON FOR FUTURE RUNS: fetch and run validate.py from the repository BEFORE publishing; do not trust the runbook's inline copy'. This run read RUNBOOK.md end to end, including its KNOWN LIMITATIONS, ran the validator embedded in it, got exit 0 on both files, and published. Only afterwards did a listing of the repository root reveal validate.py, VALIDATORS.md, STRATEGY.md and the two decisions-*.json files - none of which RUNBOOK.md mentions while describing itself as 'everything you need'. Consequence: the first IPADE publish at 13:28Z carried youGive and youGet as flat integer arrays, because that is what the runbook's Step 6 schema and its inline validator require. The repository validator requires objects with playerId, name and detail, which is also the shape the app renders, so that publish would have shown the trade player chips as holes. Caught within four minutes, converted to objects, re-validated against repo validate.py (exit 0 on both files) and republished. THE LESSON HAS NOW FAILED TWICE BECAUSE IT LIVES ONLY IN THIS LOG, which a run has no reason to open until after it has published. The fix is not another log entry: delete the inline validator from RUNBOOK.md, and add STRATEGY.md, VALIDATORS.md, validate.py and decisions-*.json to the runbook's Step 1. A warning stored downstream of the mistake cannot prevent it. THIRD DATA POINT, 16 Sep 22:15Z: the 16:00 run read the runbook first as instructed, noticed its CREDENTIALS and Step 7 sections describing an inline validator, and went to the repository root BEFORE writing anything - so the lesson did work this time, but only because the run happened to list the root early. The runbook still does not mention validate.py, STRATEGY.md, VALIDATORS.md or the decision logs. The recommended edit remains unmade and is now three runs old. FOURTH DATA POINT, 17 Sep 13:00Z: the runbook has since been amended and now names STRATEGY.md, the decision logs and validate.py in Steps 1, 4 and 7, and Step 7 instructs fetching validate.py from the repo at the start of that step rather than carrying an inline copy. This run fetched it, confirmed the 25-rule count, and both files exited 0 against it. The defect is fixed at the source; this entry is retained as the history of how three runs failed on it.

THE TRIGGER FIRED, AND IT FIRED AGAINST THE ADD. Condition written 14 Sep: 'Bowers practises in full Wednesday or carries no designation Friday, then drop Mayer before week 2. Bowers is limited or sits out Wednesday, then keep Mayer through week 2.' RotoWire, 16 September 2026: Bowers will not practise Wednesday; Klint Kubiak hopes he can go Thursday and/or Friday; he is roughly one week out from a left-knee meniscus trim and would be taking his first practice reps since. He sat out. KEEP MAYER - see ipade-drop-mayer-2026-09-14, which stands. Two process notes. First, this card was carried on 14, 15 and 16 September waiting for a session that every previous run fired too early to observe; the 16:00 CDMX run is the one that can see a Wednesday report, which is an argument for resolving practice-conditional cards in the afternoon run rather than the morning one. Second, three runs of framing drifted toward the drop branch - the 13:05 card led with 'a club expecting him to play, which is the direction that ends Mayer's role' - so the card had to resolve against its own momentum, which is a known hazard of carrying a conditional card across many runs. Hockenson remains a free agent at 62.7% rostered and is retained as a watch row; the Friday half of the trigger is still live this week, and his quarterback question resolved in his favour independently - Carson Wentz is expected to start with Kyler Murray in concussion protocol, and Wentz threw Hockenson a touchdown in the Week 1 comeback.

WRONG CHIP - the identical error this log recorded against the Team 13 offer one run earlier, repeated on the next trade without the lesson being applied. Recomputed on the 21:52Z snapshot over full rosters: Lawrence for McLaurin is +13.1 me / +3.7 Furia Regia; STAFFORD for McLaurin is +8.7 me / +8.1 them. More than double to them, for 4.4 less to me - and if the Team 13 deal lands first the two are IDENTICAL to me, both reaching 2115.4, while still paying them +8.1 against +3.7. The morning card itself described +3.7 as 'inside the range a manager declines without replying' and sent it anyway. ROOT CAUSE, same as before: the pair search was sorted by MY gain and the top row was taken as the proposal. A trade that is never accepted is worth zero, so the ranking that matters is theirs. This is now twice in two runs, which makes it a method defect rather than an oversight: the fix is to sort the pair search by the OTHER side's gain, or at minimum to check every chip that returns the same asset before choosing one. SECOND FINDING, independent of the chip: McLaurin was finally researched this run and the asset is worse than assumed - RotoWire 13 Sep have him at 2 catches on 4 targets for 14 yards while Stefon Diggs took 9 targets. Replaced by ipade-t11-stafford-mclaurin-2026-09-16-pm at odds EVEN rather than LONGSHOT, because the chip got better and the prize got worse at once.

The recorded warning stands for the future: he is now on WAIVERS here clearing 07:00Z on 20 September, so re-acquiring him before Sunday morning would cost the season's waiver priority, and that is published as a Do-not-chase row.

Yahoo's Week 2 waiver column had him as the lead back in a two-man Arizona backfield; the Week 1 split supports it at 44 snaps and 17 carries against Jeremiyah Love's 32 snaps and 13 touches. The caveat that arrived Friday and should have been in the row if it had existed: head coach Mike LaFleur, on 18 September, 'They are going to rotate. They are. This is a looong season. There are 16 more games.' Love took the Week 1 touchdown. Allgeier is the lead back by snaps, not by role, and the roster tile says so.

Sent a ninth time and retiring at Sunday kickoff rather than being rewritten again. The trade itself got BETTER tonight, not worse - Team 13's second starting running back is Rachaad White, researched for the first time this run at 27 snaps and 22 rushing yards in Week 1 against Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33 - so the row stays published as a standing offer under ipade-trade-lamar-standing-2026-09-19. What stops is the Do-first card telling him to send it again. Also corrected here: the season gain is +16.0, not +30.9.
